clue.text: Iran election possibly removing one's bigotry

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters are rearranged, while removing says one letter's worth is taken from the pool first

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Commentary on an Iranian vote that would be fair if it shed one person's prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly removing' tells you to take I (one) out of IRANELECTION and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is a refusal to tolerate other people's views or kinds, a near synonym.

clue.text: A pressing task?

parts.note: reads like an urgent job, but pressing here is pressing clothes flat with a hot iron

explanation.surface: An urgent chore that cannot wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing creases out of laundry is a household chore done with a hot iron.

clue.text: First of treasure found on ramble

indicators.note: First of takes just the opening letter of the word treasure

parts.note: to ramble or wander is to rove

explanation.surface: Treasure turned up on a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is the definition, used as a noun: what is found; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuables discovered, a find.

clue.text: Light fitting for outdoors?

parts.note: reads like an electrical fitting, but means a portable lamp suited to being carried outside

explanation.surface: An electrician's query about an outdoor lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable cased lamp is the usual light carried out of doors at night.

clue.text: Compensation from socialist on social security

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A left-winger living on benefits seeking compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is amends or reparation for a wrong suffered.

clue.text: Horrible thing with dream — headless

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Horrible thing with dream — headless (9)', appears to be missing a word (likely 'knight' for headless (K)NIGHT + MARE); no parse uses every word once

clue.text: First person in record book for example

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
the first person singular pronoun is I
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone first in the record book as a model case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'for' are link words here; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect model or typical instance of something.

clue.text: It could be you!

parts.note: sounds like a lottery slogan, but both it and you are words of the part of speech meant

explanation.surface: The National Lottery's famous advertising slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be you' was the slogan of the UK's National Lottery; 'it' and 'you' are both examples of the word class meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as it and you stand in place of a noun in grammar.

clue.text: Poser so moved with ring cycle

indicators.note: moved means the letters of poser so and ring are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A poseur emotionally stirred by Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder; 'ring cycle' pretends to be Wagner's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A progression is a series of steps or a sequence, like a cycle of chords.

clue.text: Infantile word for setters?

parts.note: setters seem to be crossword compilers, but they are the gun dogs, named in baby talk

explanation.surface: A child's name for crossword compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are a breed of dog, and toddlers call dogs by a diminutive nursery word.

clue.text: It helps to see both sides of the picture

definitions.text: It helps to see both sides of the picture

parts.words: It helps to see both sides of the picture
parts.note: sounds like fair-mindedness, but means a device showing a pair of images, one for each eye, to give depth

explanation.surface: Something that encourages balanced judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: This optical instrument merges two slightly differing photographs into a single three-dimensional view.

clue.text: Suspect deal by opposition leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of opposition is O
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Doubts about a pact struck by the Leader of the Opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not an agreement but a soft wood; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or voice a view, as one suspects something is so.

clue.text: Conductor will choose the right verse

parts.note: to elect is to choose
an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A maestro picking the correct poem for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra leader but means something carrying electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal that carries current into or out of a circuit or cell.

clue.text: Diet group losing tons

indicators.note: losing tells you the letter for tons drops out of the word for group

parts.note: a regiment is a large group, of soldiers or otherwise

explanation.surface: A slimming club shedding plenty of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of eating and exercise for health.

clue.text: Stemming a terrible charm

indicators.note: terrible suggests the words stemming a are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Holding back a dreadful spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism is an attractive power over others, much like charm.

clue.text: Cat's eye, say, is in the same area

indicators.note: in places the sound piece inside the word for the same

parts.note: same is a plain synonym of the same

indicators.note: say signals a word as heard, so eye gives its sound-alike letter

parts.note: eye is heard the same as the letter I
SE is South East, a region or area

explanation.surface: A cat's eye looks identical wherever you go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat's' reads as Cat is; 'is' is a link. SE (South East) is a region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese is a breed of slim, blue-eyed oriental feline.

clue.text: Caught and given sermon on Sunday

parts.note: to be given a sermon is to be lectured or nagged

explanation.surface: Someone caught out and lectured in church on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the lecturing after S in this across answer; 'and' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Snagged means caught on something or grabbed.

clue.text: Puritanical when church gets endless credit

parts.note: as means when
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: endless means the word for credit loses its final letter

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit

explanation.surface: Austere behaviour when the church runs up an unending tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link. Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic life is one of strict self-denial, close to puritanical austerity.

clue.text: Drive and advance slowly on river vessel

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses
to edge is to move forward slowly

explanation.surface: Instructions to steer a boat gently up a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a boat that scoops silt from riverbeds and harbours.

clue.text: They may take off seeing old bill

definitions.meaning: devices or people that strip away skin or rind
old slang for police officers, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: Things taking off at the sight of an old invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police; 'peelers' were early Victorian constables, named after Robert Peel. 'seeing' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool strips the skin from vegetables, and early British police were nicknamed after their founder.

clue.text: Irritated after party leader's toppled

indicators.note: after puts the irritation word behind the party letter
leader's takes the front letter of party

parts.note: itched means felt irritated

explanation.surface: Annoyed once the party chief was overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitched can mean fell or was thrown headlong, so toppled over.

clue.text: Former wife has a stock question

parts.note: ex is a former wife or partner
a mine is a rich stock or source, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: An ex-wife posing a query about shares.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone is to quiz or interrogate them.

clue.text: Stormy Italy's new left stick around

parts.note: I is the international code for Italy

indicators.note: around means the glue word goes outside the letter for left

parts.note: cement is a binding glue, something to stick

explanation.surface: Turbulent Italian politics as the new left hangs on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick around' looks like a phrasal verb, but stick gives CEMENT and around wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is harsh and wet, stormy.

clue.text: Divine being in opera — "Tosca" perhaps

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the words opera Tosca

explanation.surface: A goddess appearing in Puccini's opera Tosca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is a link; Tosca is just an example of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, the goddesses of the arts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Alarm has no time lapse

indicators.note: has no means the time letter is left out of the word for alarm

parts.note: terror is great alarm or fear

explanation.surface: An alarm clock that stops keeping time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or mistake.

clue.text: Seeing about Henry is of no value

indicators.note: about places the observing word around the letter for Henry

parts.note: noting is observing, seeing
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Observing a king Henry who is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth nil, a trifle, is worthless, of zero value.

clue.text: Female star of h & e

parts.note: H is drug slang for heroin
E is drug slang for ecstasy, kept as the letter

explanation.surface: A leading actress tied to hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The '&' and 'of' are links; H and E stand for drugs, and E is used as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is the principal woman character in a film, play or story.

clue.text: Closeness from dear America's uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters of dear America are unsettled and reordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Doubt about how close a dear United States really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is the warm fellowship and trust among friends.
